scene.testo: In ancient Rome, your day started before the sun did. No coffee, no alarm clock, no snooze button. You got up in the cold dark, and you dressed by feel.
Within twenty minutes, you had to be standing outside a rich man's house, in the street. Why? Because if you weren't there, you didn't eat that day.
That's not an exaggeration. That was the system. For hundreds of years, this was daily life for hundreds of thousands of ordinary Romans.
We picture togas, marble and emperors giving speeches. The reality was louder, dirtier and stranger than any movie has ever shown you.
And here's the part that breaks most people's brains. The Romans did not have hours the way you do. So how did they know when to show up? And what did they do all day?

descrizione:
What did people in ancient Rome actually do all day? Wake up before dawn and step into the daily life of an ordinary Roman citizen, from a tiny apartment to the rich man's doorstep.

In this cartoon history documentary, we explore the Roman Forum, the streets, the crowds and the strange system that decided whether you ate or went hungry. Forget the movie version of Rome: the truth was louder, dirtier and stranger.

Discover what daily life in ancient Rome was really like, and why the Romans did not measure time the way we do. Watch to the end for the surprising answer.
